mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for FEDFUNDS falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in declining FEDFUNDS periods are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals restrictive monetary policy that dampens economic growth and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In 2 years following FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for 2 months, 5-day forward returns are positive in >55% of cases, or Rank IC remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate and increase in non-farm payrolls signals a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Joint signal (UNRATE decline + PAYEMS rise) fails to produce positive 60-day returns in >55% of instances, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion, a decline in residential construction permits (HOUST) indicates cooling housing demand that signals economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion, HOUST decline does not produce negative 20-day returns in >60% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03 in that regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past 3 months indicates robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for INDPRO falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in rising INDPRO periods are not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.5% for two consecutive months, it signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer confidence and spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In 2 years following UNRATE > 5.5% for 2 months, 5-day forward returns are positive in >55% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in CPI inflation and increase in real personal consumption (RSAFS) signals stable demand environment with healthy spending, supporting equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Joint signal (CPIAUCSL decline + RSAFS rise) fails to produce positive 60-day returns in >55% of instances, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.5% YoY), a rise in federal funds rate leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as central bank tightens policy.
failure_condition: In high inflation environment (CPIAUCSL > 3.5% YoY), FEDFUNDS rise does not produce negative 20-day returns in >60% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03 in that regime.
